items.root_cause: Two mechanisms behind one alert. (1) THE RULES: fresh per-lb and per-each produce commodities refuse a FORM by literal word (\bfrozen\b on 25 of the 98 lb commodities, \bsteam\b on 3, \bcanned\b, 14\.5) but the frozen steam-bag lines are BRANDED (Green Giant Steamers, Birds Eye Steamfresh, Fareway, Season's Choice, Our Family and Simple Truth Steamable(s)) and carry no form word, so any such bag whose name contains the produce word is eligible for the fresh commodity, wins on array index over the canned or frozen commodity behind it, and stays off the cell only while the sanity band censors it or a cheaper fresh row shadows it. category-excludes.json has 18 classes and none for this shape, so every Fruit and Vegetables commodity is exposed and the blocking guard audit-food-category cannot see the class. (2) THE AUDIT: a new-contested finding is a bare name; the emailed body omits even the name; the only discriminator (CROWN-BY-CONTEST) reads cheapest_store, so a wrong product holding a non-crown cell is invisible; and 'new' means 'absent from the last -Accept snapshot', not 'never reviewed', so a one-day capture flicker re-fires reviewed contests as new (11 names on 09-07, 1 back today) while the same snapshot silently dropped MOVED and DROPPED coverage for 748 names. The memo contested-flag-baselined-away is proven live on this board: the Fareway Steamables cell is a baselined-away wrong product that no run will ever flag again under the current design.

root_fix.what: make every contested name self-describing at the moment the alert fires (chain with units, FORM tag, the engine's band verdict, whether it holds ANY store cell), put those names in the email, and stop -Accept from dropping reviewed state when a name is merely absent for a day
root_fix.exact_change: A. CELL-BY-CONTEST: generalise Get-CrownNames into Get-CellNames (every store's item on every comparison row, value 'commodity @ store per_unit per unit' plus crown true or false) and run Select-CrownByContest over that map (rename Select-CellByContest; the BELVITA fixture still fires with crown=true). Report field cell_by_contest; the console and email line says CROWN or CELL. Keep exit 1 advisory until Brad rules (open question 1). B. FORM + VERDICT per new-contested name: print the chain with each commodity's unit; tag FORM when the winner's unit differs from any loser's OR a loser id starts with canned- or frozen- while the winner's does not; look the name up in the winner commodity of the newest candidates-<date>.json and print its basis (OUT-OF-BAND, UNPRICED, or 'size X' with unit_price). Lift the alert-body construction at :458 into a function that takes the report object, and include the new-contested names WITH these tags (the console line at :449 already has the names; the email never did). C. BASELINE CARRY-FORWARD on -Accept: names present in the old baseline but absent from today's sweep are retained in names and contested, with a sibling last_seen map (name -> yyyy-MM-dd); names present today get last_seen = today; entries whose last_seen is older than 30 days expire. An old-format baseline (no last_seen) reads every entry as last_seen = its generated date. Measured on 09-07: this retains 748 names and 11 contested entries, and today's alert would not have fired as new. The MOVED and DROPPED diff loop is unchanged (it already skips names not in today's sweep).
root_fix.mechanical_discriminator: FORM + priced in band + holds a cell = money is wrong on the live board (today: fresh-green-beans at Fareway). FORM + OUT-OF-BAND or UNPRICED = latent wrong product; do not -Accept without an exclude, because bands move (Brad 2026-09-04: no hard-coded bands) and the row becomes the cell the day the fresh row is absent. Not FORM = the multi-product ad-line class (e.g. 'Hy-Vee rice, quinoa or Israeli-style couscous'), safe to accept.

items.resolution_note: Wrong product, latent at the flagged row and live at its sibling: the Green Giant Steamers bag routes to red-potatoes (kept off the cell only by the band) and 'Fareway Steamables Green Beans', a frozen 12 oz bag, routed to fresh-green-beans and held Fareway's live cell at $1.92 per lb over the fresh Pero row at $2.94 per lb, already accepted into the baseline where no run would ever flag it again. Branded frozen steam-bag lines carried no form word any Produce rule refuses. Added steam_bag_carrier to the food-class library (Produce scope) plus excludes on canned-green-beans and canned-peas: 7 names re-route, 1 cell moves (fresh-green-beans at Fareway 1.92 -> 2.94 per lb). audit-match-soundness now reads every store cell (not only the crown), tags FORM contests with the engine's band verdict, names the contested products in the email, and -Accept carries absent names forward so a one-day capture flicker can no longer re-fire a reviewed contest (11 lost on 09-07, 1 back today) or drop MOVED and DROPPED coverage (748 names on 09-07). The 7th artifact name ('Green Giant Steamers Lightly Sauced Roasted Red Potatoes, Green Beans & Rosemary') cannot appear as a DROPPED line because it is not in the baseline to be dropped FROM - the 2026-09-07 -Accept erased it - and it shows instead as a pre-rebuild DRIFT line, then as drift=0 after the rebuild, which is the same fact. (3) THE ONE MOVING CELL - FALSE AS WRITTEN, TRUE AS ATTRIBUTED. The rebuild moved NINE cells, not one. Attribution measured, not assumed: of the 17 item names on those 9 cells exactly ONE carries a steam-bag token ('Fareway Steamables Green Beans'), and an exclude-only change can only move a cell whose item it removed; none of the other 8 cells sits in any of the 8 commodities where a removed name was a candidate, so second-order capture selection cannot reach them either. Every one of those 8 belongs to Aldi, Walmart or Family Fare - exactly the three stores whose captures landed after 08:07 - with zero residue. fresh-green-beans @ Fareway moved 1.92 'Fareway Steamables Green Beans' -> 2.94 'Pero Family Farms Snipped Green Beans', crown unchanged at Walmart 1.6201, exactly as planned. audit-capture-eviction: 0 cells dearer than the eligibility rule allows, so the 2026-08-06 eviction class did not fire. (4) CARRY-FORWARD - THE MECHANISM WORKS, THE RESTORE CLAIM IS FALSE. Today's -Accept retained 249 names and 1 contested entry that the old code would have erased by absence, wrote a last_seen map of 19,354 entries (19,105 dated today, 249 dated 2026-09-07), and expired 0. It does NOT restore the entries the 2026-09-07 -Accept already deleted, and it cannot: it reads the CURRENT baseline, which no longer contains them. The 10 still-absent entries will each fire as new-contested once when they return, be reviewed under the new FORM and verdict tags, and be protected from then on. match-baseline.json was NOT hand-edited, per do_not_touch.
items.deviation: FIVE deviations, all gated the same way as the plan items. (A) A SECOND WRONG PRODUCT, FOUND BY THIS BATCH'S OWN CLASS FIX AND FIXED IN IT. The new FORM tag fired on its first live run: 'HORMEL Chili Cilantro Lime with Beans, 15 oz Can' routed to cilantro (each) over canned-chili (oz), tagged FORM, engine verdict UNPRICED. That is the plan's own mechanical_discriminator saying do not -Accept without an exclude, so cilantro.exclude += '\bchili\b' (narrow: it cannot match a fresh cilantro bunch, and \b stops it matching 'Chilies', so 'Hy-Vee Mexican Lime & Cilantro Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies' is untouched). A/B over identical inputs: the board was rebuilt with only this exclude changed and the cell diff was EMPTY, 0 cells moved, which is what UNPRICED predicted. Not a brand block, per the seller-shape rule. (B) GUARDS WAS ALREADY RED BEFORE THIS RUN, on a row this run did not create. guards.ps1 hard-failed 1 invariant: multipack size, [Aldi] 'Peach Iced Functional Teas 4pk' size=[16 fl oz] records ONE unit. It entered with the Aldi capture written at 09:16, after the 08:07 board, and nothing had re-run guards since. Test-MpClassify verdict 'reject', Get-MpRepairedSize '' (the name states no per-unit weight), so the sanctioned lane is multipack-unit-hints.json, which is exactly how plan-2026-09-03 cleared the same shape at the same store. Corroborated twice before writing the hint, as that precedent requires: every other pack row in the same capture carries the 'N pk M unit' form and this is the only bare per-unit measure; and Aldi's own listing puts a peach iced tea bottle at 16 fl oz (slug '21306159-benner-diet-peach-tea-16-fl-oz', sold as a 6 pack; the functional 'Iced Tea with Benefits, Peach' is likewise 16 fl oz). Aldi lists no 4 fl oz tea bottle. Repaired through the shared multipack-lib math to '4 pk 16 fl oz' = 64 fl oz, $0.0936/floz against the $0.3744 the raw row implied. Board diff over the repair: 0 cells moved. NO GUARD, THRESHOLD OR FIXTURE WAS TOUCHED - the data was repaired and guards then read hard=0 on its own. (C) A DEFECT IN THIS ITEM'S OWN FIRST CUT, found by running it. Building the report with $report['key'] = @(...) on an [ordered] dictionary throws ArgumentException 'Argument types do not match' in PS 5.1 once the dictionary is non-empty and the value is an object[]; under EAP=Stop that killed the script before its first line of output, so it read as a crash rather than a typed-assignment fault. Reproduced standalone, reverted to the [ordered]@{} literal the original used, and the mechanism is written into the source above the line. (D) FORMAT: the cell description keeps the existing '<id> @ <store> <per_unit>/<unit>' form ('fresh-green-beans @ Fareway 1.92/lb') rather than the plan's prose 'per unit' wording, so the frozen BELVITA assertion stays byte-identical and is not rewritten while its subject is being generalised. (E) CHAIN: ran the full mid-day rebuild sequence from [[compare-deals-is-not-standalone]] (compare-deals -IdentityNamespace staple, recipe-overlay, prune-bad-links -Tol 0.32, sync-browser-links, audit-name-drift, audit-capture-eviction) rather than the plan's shorter list, because compare-deals alone leaves the board inconsistent with product-urls.json. relink-drifted-cells reports 175 pre-existing drifted tiles across all 7 stores and exits 1 advisory; it is not this change's doing and audit-name-drift is exit 0.

items.subject: Ops: the agent memory store has a finding
evidence: audit-memory-backup.ps1 reports 25 of 190 memory files reachable by neither MEMORY.md nor a one-hop [[wikilink]] from an indexed memo. The orchestrator re-ran the census independently: FILES=190 LINKED=126 DIRECT=126 HUB=39 UNREACHABLE=25. The guard's count is correct - this is NOT the 2026-09-05 false-positive class where all 64 reported orphans were really hub-routed.
17 of the 25 are linked by NO memo at all; the other 8 are linked only by other unreachable memos, which the guard's deliberate one-hop rule correctly declines to count as recall.

Cause located in the memory store's own git history. Commits cd14520 and fcbacf2 (both 2026-09-07, 'Eleven episodes faded to pointers' and 'The seven deferred clusters are cleared') rewrote four HUB memos down to ~1.1KB pointers: guard-blindness-family.md 6289 -> 1082 bytes (26 wikilinks -> 0), repair-sweep-hazards.md 3440 -> 1085 (12 -> 0), board-match-collisions.md 27410 -> 1308 (10 -> 0), same-fact-published-twice.md 5598 -> 1171 (13 -> 5). 56 routing links deleted.

The causal match is exact with zero residue: every one of the 25 unreachable memos is a memo whose ONLY route was one of those 56 deleted links. The two hubs NOT touched on 2026-09-07 (board-basis-ambiguity.md 12801 bytes, accuracy-program-built.md 8303 bytes) still carry their 'Routed from the index' sections, and none of their children are orphaned.
items.root_cause: A consolidation pass that fades a hub memo's episode down to a pointer rewrites the file wholesale and takes its 'Routed from the index' section with it. In this store a HUB IS THE ONLY INDEX LINE ITS CHILDREN HAVE - that is MEMORY.md's documented convention - so deleting a hub's routing orphans every child instantly, and the writer gets no feedback at the moment of the edit. Nothing in the store distinguishes 'this memo's prose was summarised' from 'this memo's routing was deleted', and the hub-reachability count that would have shown it (64ish -> 39) has no stored baseline, so the drop was invisible until it crossed into outright unreachability a day later.

surface_fix.what: restore the 'Routed from the index' sections to the four hub memos so all 25 memos are reachable again, keeping the 2026-09-07 consolidation intact
surface_fix.exact_change: KEEP the 2026-09-07 consolidation - the pointer to skills/data-quality-craft/applies-here.md and the faded episode text stay; only the deleted routing links come back. Recover the prior 'Routed from the index' sections with git -C C:\Users\Owner\.claude\projects\C--Codex\memory show 4041025:<file> (and e2a8760:<file> for repair-sweep-hazards.md and same-fact-published-twice.md) and re-append them. That store is its OWN local git repo with a reviewed private remote: commit there, and NEVER let a memory file become tracked by ThriftyCrew (this repo is PUBLIC).

root_fix.what: make the guard publish its whole worklist with the right remedy, and add a reachability REGRESSION arm that fires at the moment a hub edit orphans a memo instead of a day later
root_fix.exact_change: 1. The alert names only the FIRST FIVE of 25 unreachable files and its 'Fix:' line prescribes only -Sync, removing a remote, or untracking a leaked file - none of which does anything for unreachability. An alert that publishes 20% of its own worklist and then prescribes the wrong remedy is why 25 accumulated instead of being cleared on day one. Print EVERY unreachable name (it is the actionable worklist), and give the unreachability arm its own accurate remedy sentence naming hub routing as the fix. 2. Add a REACHABILITY REGRESSION arm. The store is a git repo, so this is cheap: compare reachability at HEAD against the previous commit, and report by name any memo that WAS reachable and is now not, naming the hub whose link disappeared. That converts 'a consolidation silently orphaned 25 memos and nobody could tell for a day' into a finding that cannot ship quiet, and it is the arm that fires at the moment of the edit rather than a day later.

items.deviation: TWO deviations, neither changing the outcome the plan asked for. (A) 'Routed from the index' IS NOT THE SECTION NAME IN TWO OF THE FOUR FILES. Only board-match-collisions.md and same-fact-published-twice.md carry a literal '## Routed from the index' heading; guard-blindness-family.md routes its 26 children under four ARM headings and repair-sweep-hazards.md routes its 11 under four numbered questions. So the restore recovered the ROUTING REGION of each prior revision rather than a heading by name: guard-blindness-family 4041025 lines 16-88, repair-sweep-hazards e2a8760 lines 16-48, board-match-collisions 4041025 lines 201-222, same-fact-published-twice e2a8760 lines 50-76. Committed and pushed in the memory store's OWN repo (290e8920), never staged into ThriftyCrew - re-verified after the push: 0 memory files tracked here. (B) THE REGRESSION ARM COMPARES THE FILES ON DISK against the previous commit, not HEAD against HEAD~1 as the plan words it. Check 4 already requires a clean tree, so in the healthy case they are the same comparison; in a dirty tree this one still looks, which is strictly more coverage and no less. It reads the previous tree with ONE `git grep` for wikilink-bearing lines rather than 126 `git show` calls, because a guard that costs 126 process spawns is a guard someone switches off. A previous commit that cannot be read is recorded as a NOTE, never as silence. items.subject: Discovered in-run: both triage agent definitions resolve memory hooks to the WRONG store and then disown the right one
evidence: triage-reviewer.md and triage-developer.md both resolved [[wikilink]] hooks to '~/.claude/projects/C--Codex-ThriftyCrew/memory/<filename>' and both closed with 'Regime: the path above is this machine's store for THIS project. C--Codex and C--Codex-income are different projects with their own stores, and nothing in them applies here.'

That is backwards for this chain. A store is named for the directory the SESSION was launched from; the triage orchestrator runs from C:\Codex, so its store is C--Codex. Measured on disk: C--Codex\memory holds 191 .md files, C--Codex-ThriftyCrew\memory holds 140. ops\audit-memory-backup.ps1 hardcodes C--Codex, and queue item 2026-09-08-231ef6 was a repair TO C--Codex.

It cost real work twice today. The reviewer had to append 'note: that memo is in the C--Codex store, not the C--Codex-ThriftyCrew store my definition points to' when citing contested-flag-baselined-away. The developer reported 'a scoping tension worth your ruling: my own definition marks the agent memory store READ-ONLY, naming C--Codex-ThriftyCrew ... Item 2 required writing to C--Codex' and had to adjudicate its own permissions mid-run.

triage-developer.md was additionally self-contradictory: line 114 instructed it to record a new failure class in C:\Users\Owner\.claude\projects\C--Codex\memory\ while line 230 said READ-ONLY, never write there, and line 234 said C--Codex does not apply here.

Scope measured before editing: the same two lines appear in 20 definition files across C:\Users\Owner\.claude\agents and C:\Codex\ThriftyCrew\.claude\agents. They are CORRECT in the 16 recipe-agent copies, which are launched from C:\Codex\ThriftyCrew and really do get the C--Codex-ThriftyCrew store. Only the 2 triage definitions are wrong.
items.root_cause: A definition hardcodes ONE literal store path as though the memory store were a property of the AGENT. It is not - it is a property of the CWD the session was launched from. One literal path therefore cannot be correct for both the recipe agents (launched from C:\Codex\ThriftyCrew) and the triage agents (launched from C:\Codex), so copying the line between definitions silently points half of them at a store that is not theirs, and the accompanying Regime sentence then actively instructs the reader to disregard the store its hooks actually live in.

surface_fix.what: point both triage definitions at C--Codex, and carve the developer out of the blanket READ-ONLY rule for a memory-store change its own gated plan item prescribes
surface_fix.exact_change: resolver path -> C:\Users\Owner\.claude\projects\C--Codex\memory\<filename>; developer READ-ONLY paragraph gains the plan-item exception plus the two standing rules (never git add a memory file into the PUBLIC ThriftyCrew repo, never add a remote to the store)

root_fix.what: replace the literal-path Regime sentence with the RULE that derives it, so the next definition copied from these cannot inherit a wrong path: a store is C-- plus the launch cwd with separators flattened, derive it from the launch cwd rather than copying a path out of another agent definition. The paragraph names both concrete stores and says which sessions get which, so the recipe agents reading the same wording stay right.
root_fix.exact_change: Regime paragraph rewritten to state the derivation rule plus the 2026-09-08 account of what the old wording cost

blast_radius.measured_by: prose-only change to 2 agent definitions in 2 locations each; no board input, no rule, no engine path is read by these files. Verified the 16 recipe-agent definitions still carry their (correct) C--Codex-ThriftyCrew resolver: 8 files x 2 matches each, unchanged.
blast_radius.risk: none to the board. The failure mode of the edit itself would be a mangled definition, which is checked directly: no BOM, zero CRLF introduced, YAML frontmatter still opens with ---, and the two copies of each file re-hashed byte-identical so they cannot silently diverge.

items.freshness: not board-dependent. Verified against the definitions as they stood at HEAD 45dcd1722 on 2026-09-08.

proof.guard_or_fixture: the applier scratchpad\fix-triage-store-path.ps1 asserts its own preconditions and postconditions and exits nonzero rather than writing
proof.must_fire_case: each of the 3 substitutions must match EXACTLY ONCE before any write; 0 or 2 matches refuses the file and exits 1. This fired for real on the first run: an over-broad postcondition (any mention of the string C--Codex-ThriftyCrew) refused all 4 files and wrote nothing, which is the correct behaviour for a check that cannot tell a resolver path from prose naming the other store.
proof.clean_twin: the 16 recipe-agent definitions must come through untouched, still resolving to C--Codex-ThriftyCrew, or the fix has overreached into agents for which the old line was correct. Verified after the run: 8 recipe files, 2 matches each, unchanged.

do_not_touch: the 16 recipe-agent definitions, whose C--Codex-ThriftyCrew resolver is correct for the cwd they launch from
the two standing memory rules: no remote, and never tracked by the PUBLIC ThriftyCrew repo
items.resolution_note: Found during STEP 5 verification, not by an alert. Both triage agent definitions resolved memory hooks to C--Codex-ThriftyCrew and then declared C--Codex "a different project ... nothing in them applies here", which is inverted for a chain launched from C:\Codex; it cost the reviewer a workaround note and made the developer adjudicate its own write permission mid-run. Both now name C--Codex, the developer has an explicit carve-out for a memory-store change its gated plan item prescribes, and the Regime sentence now states the derivation rule instead of a literal path so a definition copied from these cannot inherit the wrong store. The 16 recipe definitions were measured as correct and deliberately left alone.
items.premise_verified: true - verified on disk before editing: C--Codex\memory 191 files, C--Codex-ThriftyCrew\memory 140 files, and the two triage definitions were byte-identical duplicates (SHA256 6203AAA1...) across both agent directories.
items.deviation: The first applier run refused all four files and wrote nothing, because its postcondition forbade the string C--Codex-ThriftyCrew anywhere while the new Regime prose deliberately names that store to say which sessions get it. Narrowed the assertion to the actual invariant (no projects/C--Codex-ThriftyCrew/memory RESOLVER PATH) and re-ran. No partial write occurred: the check runs before WriteAllText.
